subject: Control crosswalk and evidence lane for FinGate RFI
messages:
From: FinGate Procurement <procure@fingate.com>
To: soojin_lee@redwood.example.com
Cc: Alan Cho <alan.cho@fingate.com>
Date: 2026-11-22T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: RFI: control mapping and evidence lane request

Hi Soojin,

Thanks for taking the RFI. Our procurement team is consolidating supplier evidence for the upcoming FinGate vendor review. Can you provide a control crosswalk mapping Redwood controls to the Consensus/SIG schema and a preliminary evidence inventory for SOC 2 and ISO 27001 controls?

Key constraints:
- We need a mapping for the subset of controls related to crypto custody, KMS, and data residency by 2026-11-30.
- For any controls that rely on third-party cloud services, please call out compensating controls and the responsible owner.
- Attachments preferred as a single workbook plus an evidence CSV.

Would appreciate a short runbook or artifact list we can pass to our audit team.

Regards,
--
FinGate Procurement
procure@fingate.com
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.example.com>
To: FinGate Procurement <procure@fingate.com>
Cc: neha_kapoor@redwood.example.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.example.com, jonas_weber@redwood.example.com
Date: 2026-11-22T11:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: RFI: control mapping and evidence lane request

Hi Maya / Alan / procurement team,

Thanks — we can deliver a crosswalk and a short evidence runbook by tomorrow close of business PT. Attached is our initial package: redwood_fingate_control-crosswalk_v1.xlsx and evidence_inventory_v1.csv. The workbook includes three sheets: (1) Consensus->Redwood control mapping, (2) evidence owner and artifact name, (3) gaps and recommended compensating controls.

High-level notes:
- Data residency: Hosted product is available in us-west and eu-west regions. Customer can pin region via the account config; we flagged controls that depend on regional deployment.
- KMS: We use customer-managed keys (CMK) on Dedicated/Private plans; hosted customers use Redwood-managed KMS (AWS KMS) with quarterly rotation. See row C-KEY-01 in the crosswalk.
- SOC 2 artifacts: SOC 2 Type II report (summary link in the runbook), access review logs (audit_log_YYYYMM.csv), and our change-control runbook are referenced in the evidence CSV.

Next steps we propose:
1) Please review the attached crosswalk and confirm which control IDs you want substantiated first (crypto custody and KMS controls recommended).
2) If helpful, we can do a 30m technical deep-dive with your security team mid-next week to walk artifacts and open items.

Attachments: redwood_fingate_control-crosswalk_v1.xlsx (workbook), evidence_inventory_v1.csv (artifact index)

Best,
--
Soojin Lee
Head of Assurance Programs
Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.example.com
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.example.com>
To: soojin_lee@redwood.example.com
Cc: neha_kapoor@redwood.example.com, jonas_weber@redwood.example.com, FinGate Procurement <procure@fingate.com>
Date: 2026-11-23T08:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: RFI: control mapping and evidence lane request

Maya / team — following up with technical clarifications that will appear in v2 of the crosswalk:

1) KMS key rotation: Hosted (Redwood-managed KMS) rotates root keys quarterly; customers on Dedicated with CMK can bring their own rotation policies. We'll attach a redacted kms-rotation-policy.pdf to show process and evidence of rotation events.

2) Crypto custody controls: Our SDKs do not persist private keys; customer-managed keying for private deployments remains the recommended model. For hosted customers who push signing operations to Redwood, we list compensating controls (ephemeral signing, limited HSM session timeouts, per-tenant request quotas). See controls C-CRYPTO-02 and C-CRYPTO-05 in the workbook.

3) Egress and data export: We have an egress audit flag (audit_log_egress.csv) and a policy that requires approval for exports containing PHI/PII. We can provide a sanitized sample export request ticket if needed.

Action items for FinGate: please indicate whether you require HSM attestation (FIPS 140-2/3) for any workload; that will change which artifacts we surface.

I'll update the crosswalk with exact evidence pointers (S3 path + manifest) and include the rotation PDF in v2.

Thanks,
--
Karthik Iyer
Director, Infrastructure Security
Redwood Inference
From: Maya Singh (FinGate Security) <maya.singh@fingate.com>
To: soojin_lee@redwood.example.com
Cc: Alan Cho <alan.cho@fingate.com>, procure@fingate.com
Date: 2026-11-25T16:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: RFI: control mapping and evidence lane request

Thanks Soojin / Karthik — we reviewed v1 and a few clarifying asks before the deep-dive: 

- For C-KEY-01 and C-CRYPTO-02 please include the S3 manifest path for the last 12 months of rotation events and a redacted sample KMS audit log showing the rotation API calls.
- For the hosted encryption model, confirm whether envelope encryption is used and provide the key-wrapping algorithm (e.g., RSA-OAEP-256).
- Please flag any controls that are marked as "compensating" and include the exact compensating artifacts. For example, for ephemeral signing, provide sample logs showing ephemeral key creation and expiry.

We can take the 30m deep-dive on 2026-11-29 at 10:00 PT — Alan from Legal will sit in for contract alignment. Can Redwood share the updated workbook and the kms-rotation-policy.pdf before the call?

Best regards,
--
Maya Singh
Senior Security Engineer, FinGate
maya.singh@fingate.com
